freshness_rule: Nothing older than 7 days is published; undated items are dropped; flights are positions from this run (each at most 15 minutes old when fetched).

chokepoints.name: Strait of Hormuz
chokepoints.why: The narrow gap between Iran and Oman that oil tankers from Saudi Arabia, Iraq, the UAE, Kuwait and Qatar sail through — commonly cited as around a fifth of the world's oil consumption.

chokepoints.why: The strait between Yemen and Djibouti linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden; the route to and from the Suez Canal for Asia-Europe trade and Gulf oil.

chokepoints.why: The main sea route between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea, between Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore — one of the world's busiest shipping lanes.

chokepoints.why: Separates Taiwan from mainland China; a flashpoint for semiconductor supply chains (Taiwan makes most of the world's advanced chips) and regional security.
